thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Hosted API p95/p99 latency spike and queue growth in us-east-1. Autoscaler failing to provision GPU capacity. Automated mitigations attempted and failed. Details: 30m ago traffic jump, queue growth > 10k, p95 ~ 3s -> 18s, p99 ~ 12s -> 45s. Firing page to #incidents.

robert (oncall): Seeing it, paging in. I'm jumping in now. Any idea if this is customer-driven surge or system loop? :eyes:

sam (sre): Early indicators point to a small set of clients (IP ranges) sending large batch bursts. Provisioner logs show quota API 429s when creating new thin-provision GPU pools.

jia (runtime): Runtime reports KV-cache churn high, many cold contexts. We're seeing continuous batching backpressure - worker pods are saturated and falling back to queueing.

oliver (provisioner): Confirming quota 429s from cloud provider in provisioner. Rate limit + per-region GPU limit hit. Provisioner retried and hit exponential backoff; new pools not created.

robert (oncall): Ok, immediate plan: 1) throttle offending clients at ingress, 2) temporarily disable automatic batching to reduce per-request pressure, 3) spin up a manual spare GPU pool (if quota allows) and pin critical customers to it. Who can run manual pool?

oliver (provisioner): I can attempt manual pool creation but same quota limits will apply. I can request quota bump, but that's slow. Alternative: reassign some Dedicated capacity from staging to hosted as emergency.

sam (sre): Throttling rule deployed to edge: rate-limit header applied for top 5 offending API keys (identified). Should cut incoming spike by ~60% within next 30s.

maya (cs): Heads-up: Customer A is one of the heavy hitters and is probably impacted. CC'ing account team. We'll prepare a proactive message if we see errors.

robert (oncall): Deploy-bot, can you apply fallback routing to route low-priority traffic to smaller quantized model? We need to preserve capacity for customers with SLA.

deploy-bot: exec: applying route policy 'sla-preserve-2026-03-15'

Applied: low-priority tag -> model-q4-small in us-east-1.

jia (runtime): Fallback routing applied. We're seeing immediate drop in p95 for SLA-tagged routes. Overall p95 improved from 18s -> 9s, p99 45s -> 26s. Queue length still high (~6k).

sam (sre): Provisioner metrics: request backlog for new pools stalled due to provider-side global limit. We have an open support case but ETA unknown.

oliver (provisioner): As a backup, I initiated an emergency rebind of 4 GPUs from staging to hosted. This will reduce staging throughput but should give ~30% extra capacity. Triggered manual migration now.

robert (oncall): Noted. Once migration completes, we'll re-evaluate autoscaler thresholds so it doesn't overshoot re-create loops. Also need to check eviction policy that caused too-aggressive caching invalidation under load.

sam (sre): I pushed a quick autoscaler patch to reduce retry backoff and add jitter to reduce synchronized retries. Patch will land in 2m.

jia (runtime): Also disabling continuous batching for the next 10m to reduce KV cache churn. Command: `./admin runtime set-batching --mode none --duration 10m`

robert (oncall): Good. CS, prepare status update: impacted requests ~8% of total, error rate 504/429 spike for impacted keys ~12%, degraded latency for 22% of tenants. Maya, can you draft a short customer note? Keep it high level, apologize, note mitigations.

maya (cs): Drafting now. Will post to #customer-notifications in 10m once current mitigations show improvement.

sam (sre): Autoscaler patch merged and rolled; provisioner backoff now randomized. Early signs: provisioner retry rate down 70%, some queued create requests moving through.

oliver (provisioner): Manual GPU rebinding complete. New capacity online, routing adjusted. Queue length falling: 6k -> 1.4k over 4m. p95 now 2.2s, p99 6.8s.

robert (oncall): Great. We're out of immediate danger but need postmortem and follow-ups: - fix autoscaler retry/backoff config, - add regional soft-quotas and graceful degrade path when provider returns 429, - pre-provision emergency buffer capacity for hosted critical SLAs, - improve ingress detection to throttle noisy clients earlier.

sam (sre): I'll own autoscaler backoff change and tests. Jira: INF-4852.

jia (runtime): I'll own graceful degrade/quantized fallback tuning. Jira: INF-4853.

oliver (provisioner): I'll follow up with cloud provider support for quota increase and add pre-warm flows. Jira: INF-4854.

maya (cs): Customer notification queued, awaiting final metrics. Will escalate to account teams for top impacted customers.

robert (oncall): Oncall handoff in 45m — I'll prepare summary for nightshift. Current status: degraded -> stabilizing, manual mitigations applied, capacity restored via manual rebinding, autoscaler adjusted. Will mark incident as mitigated in 30m if no regression.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigations recorded. Runbook snapshot attached: /runbooks/hosted/rapid-surge-mitigation (internal).

robert (oncall): Thanks team. Keep monitoring; update this thread with any regressions.

maya (cs): Posted customer note at 5543219950: "We experienced a service degradation in us-east-1 due to an unexpected traffic spike; mitigation in progress; some requests returned errors or experienced higher latency. We're working on restoring full service and will follow up with details."

sam (sre): Logging follow-up action items and scheduling postmortem.

robert (oncall): Last check-in: p95 1.9s, p99 4.1s, queue ~420. I'll transition to monitoring-only. Handoff to night oncall: @alex (oncall-night).

end of thread
